requirement:
`habeas status`, and `habeas author` after it finishes, MUST report the number
of nodes without recent coverage under
{cite}`requirements.references.coverage.history`, except items inside a module
named `tests`, using the following summary:

```text
N nodes have coverage warnings. Use `status --coverage` to see them.
```

The summary MUST report zero when no nodes have warnings. Default output MUST
NOT list individual coverage warnings or coverage-history details, including
with `status --all` or `status --verbose`.
`habeas status --coverage` MUST list every warning, naming its file, line, kind,
and name, and report incomplete coverage history when applicable.
A warning MUST NOT fail validation, and repository validation MUST NOT read
Git history.
rationale:
The reviewed tests adequately cover every obligation in `requirements.references.coverage.report`.

- **Summary line in `habeas status`.**
  - `tests/commands.rs#fn[status_preserves_repository_wide_rust_findings_in_every_form]` runs the real CLI. It uses default, `--all`, `--verbose` and `--all --verbose`, each with and without a selection. It asserts the "N nodes have coverage warnings. Use `status --coverage` to see them." line. It also asserts that the text has no "has no recent coverage" and no `## Coverage warnings` heading.
  - `tests/coverage.rs#fn[status_shows_coverage_warnings_and_says_when_history_is_incomplete]` asserts the count line and the absence of detail lines in default status.
- **Summary line in `habeas author`.**
  - `tests/coverage.rs#fn[habeas_author_prints_only_the_coverage_warning_count_on_stderr]` runs the binary and asserts the count on stderr. It also asserts that no warning details and no history-incomplete text appear on stderr or stdout.
  - The `tests/authoring_batch.rs` tests assert the same summary after batch runs, single-subject runs, `--stdout` runs and runs that skip current records. They also assert that no history-incomplete text appears and that the orphan function is not listed.
- **Zero case.** `tests/coverage.rs#fn[incomplete_history_is_noted_even_with_nothing_to_warn_about]` asserts "0 nodes have coverage warnings…" in default status. It also asserts that the incomplete-history note is absent from default status.
- **No history details in default output, including `--all` and `--verbose`.**
  - The `fixture()` project in `tests/commands.rs` is not a Git repository, so its history is incomplete. The `--all` and `--verbose` runs therefore exercise the incomplete case.
  - The incomplete note is rendered inside `coverage_section` under the `## Coverage warnings` heading, which the test asserts is absent.
  - I read `coverage_section` only to confirm where the note is printed. It is not what the requirement is derived from.
- **`status --coverage` lists every warning with file, line, kind and name.**
  - The `tests/commands.rs` test asserts a `file:line: function unread has no recent coverage…` entry in every flag and selection combination.
  - The `tests/coverage.rs` status test asserts the `render` entry with its file and line. It also asserts that `parse` is not listed once it is covered.
  - `coverage_lasts_for_three_reauthorings_of_the_record_that_read_an_item` asserts exact warned name lists, which covers "every" warning.
  - `items_in_out_of_line_tests_modules_are_not_warned_about` asserts the exact full set of warned names.
- **Incomplete history in `status --coverage`.** The shallow-clone tests assert "Coverage history is incomplete" under `--coverage`. They also assert its absence when history is complete.
  - `status_shows_coverage_warnings_and_says_when_history_is_incomplete` and `incomplete_history_is_noted_even_with_nothing_to_warn_about` cover the incomplete case.
  - `a_shallow_clone_holding_every_window_is_complete` covers the complete case.
- **Exclusion of items inside `tests` modules.**
  - `src/coverage_history.rs#mod[tests]/fn[files_declared_as_tests_modules_are_in_a_tests_module]` checks the path classification, both positive and negative.
  - `items_in_out_of_line_tests_modules_are_not_warned_about` checks out-of-line `tests.rs` and `tests/mod.rs`.
  - `src/rust_coverage.rs#mod[tests]/fn[a_test_without_a_test_reference_is_an_error_not_a_coverage_warning]` checks that a bare `#[test]` is an error while a plain helper is only a warning.
  - `coverage_lasts_for_three_reauthorings_of_the_record_that_read_an_item` covers the inline `mod tests` fixture.
- **Warnings do not fail validation.**
  - `coverage_lasts_for_three_reauthorings_of_the_record_that_read_an_item` asserts that validation reports no error mentioning `parse`.
  - The `tests/commands.rs` test asserts that `status --coverage` exits successfully.
  - The `tests/authoring_batch.rs` tests `batch_authors_citation_reviews_and_preserves_current_ones` and `missing_keeps_current_records_and_force_reassesses_every_selected_subject` assert empty validation errors despite warnings.
- **Validation does not read Git history.** `tests/coverage.rs#fn[validation_does_not_read_git_history]` deletes the Git object store. It then asserts that validation errors are unchanged while coverage warnings report incomplete history.
- **Examples.** `coverage.reauthored` and `coverage.new_function` are covered by `coverage_lasts_for_three_reauthorings_of_the_record_that_read_an_item`. It asserts no warning for `parse` in rounds 1 and 2 and a warning after round 3. It also asserts a warning for `helper` at once.
- **Consistency of the warning inventory.** `src/commands.rs#mod[tests]/fn[coverage_warning_inventory_matches_full_inspection_with_invalid_evidence]` checks that the fast and full warning inventories match when evidence is invalid or missing.

I found no unacknowledged gap. The window semantics and `reauthorings` setting belong to `coverage.history` and are not assessed here.

`habeas status`, and `habeas author` after it finishes, MUST report the number
of nodes without recent coverage under
{cite}`requirements.references.coverage.history`, except items inside a module
named `tests`, using the following summary:
```text
N nodes have coverage warnings. Use `status --coverage` to see them.
The summary MUST report zero when no nodes have warnings. Default output MUST
NOT list individual coverage warnings or coverage-history details, including
with `status --all` or `status --verbose`.

:::{req} coverage.history
{impl}`requirements.configuration.feature_sections`
An item has recent coverage when it has a reference that covers it under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`, or when its outline node, or
an outline node containing it, is named by file and selector in the inputs of
any version of an existing evidence record, citation review, or site review in
its coverage window. A file's coverage window MUST be its current contents on
disk, committed or not, together with its contents in each of the last N
commits in its Git history that changed it, read through a Git library rather
than by running `git`. A recorded hash MUST NOT matter here: an earlier version
names the node, whatever its code was then. N MUST be the workspace
`[coverage]` setting `reauthorings`, a positive integer, and 3 when it is not
set. When the history is unavailable, such as outside Git or in a shallow clone
missing those commits, the window MUST be the commits that are available, and
`habeas status --coverage` MUST say that coverage history is incomplete.
:::{example} coverage.reauthored
Function `parse` has no reference, and the evidence of `requirements.cli.check`
read it. The requirement is re-authored and committed twice, and neither new
record reads `parse`. With the default window of 3, the record's third most
recent version still names `parse`, so `habeas status --coverage` does not warn.
After a third such commit, no version in the window names it, and
`habeas status --coverage` warns about `parse`.
{test}`requirements.references.coverage.history`
{test}`requirements.references.coverage.report`
:::{example} coverage.new_function
A new function `helper` has no reference, and no evidence record has ever read
it. `habeas status --coverage` warns about it at once; nothing in any window
names it.
{test}`requirements.references.coverage.report`
:::{example} coverage.test_module
A helper function inside `mod tests` has no reference and is read by no record.
`habeas status --coverage` does not warn about it. A `#[test]` function in the
same module without a `{test}` reference is still a validation error.
{test}`requirements.references.coverage.report`
{test}`requirements.references.coverage.tests`
